findings.summary: Test gap: the new wiring has no test in the diff. That covers `init.ts` (it reads `resume.developerRound` and passes `resumeFeedback`), `next-step.ts` (`developerRoundPending`, `consumeDeveloperRound` in `onDeveloper`, and the follow-up `decideResumeReview`), and `cli/dispatch.ts` (`predictResumePath` and the `resumePath` output). Acceptance criterion 2 and criterion 3 are exercised only at the unit level, in `decideResumeReview` and `consumeDeveloperRound`. The regression to guard against is `onDeveloper` no longer consuming the flag, which would force a developer round on every later resume. Please add a next-step machine test: a resumed task with the flag set runs the developer, clears the flag, then picks delta or unchanged. Add a CLI test for the printed `resumePath`.

findings.summary: `--developer-round` is silently ignored when `reenter` returns a non-manifest result (refused, or a note-less green PR). No `resumePath` is printed, so dispatch can believe a round was ordered when it was not. Consider surfacing a warning in that case. Separately, `predictResumePath` casts a partial object to `NextStepContext`; this works today because `decide` only uses `runner` and `workDir`, but it is fragile if `decide` later reads `ctx.logger` or `ctx.env`.
